correctness.rationale: For every connected simple cactus, gradients form an orthogonal product of bridge coordinates and one central cube section per edge-disjoint cycle. The uniform law factors because the incidence-map Jacobian is constant. Bridge gradient variance equals 1/3; cycle exchangeability yields a_r P and f_{r-1} evaluates a_r exactly. Congruence inversion proves precision L_w on 1-perp, positive w recovers labeled edges, and matrix-tree gives determinant. A Fourier Laplace ratio gives a_r = 1/3 + 1/(5r)+O(r^-2). Independent exact rational weighted Ehrhart moments verify all entries, determinant and support on seven graphs n<=6; they are not an infinite proof. A direct conditional disintegration on K2,3 gives covariance eigenvalues 2/15, 2/9 and 4/45 and inverse precision nonedge (0,2) = -3/8; independent weighted Ehrhart checks confirm its full exact precision matrix.

value.rationale: This is a broad structural theorem for every unit cactus graph, not one finite numerical invariant. It gives an exact non-Gaussian covariance precision with the same edge support as the underlying graph, reconstructs its labeled topology from population covariance, provides rational edge conductances and determinant in closed form, and resolves the large-cycle conductance regime. Covariance precision sparsity is not automatic for general non-Gaussian polytope measures. Relevant graph-circle and random Lipschitz literature makes the invariant mathematically natural. The exact K2,3 non-cactus counterexample proves this sparse-precision geometry is genuinely not universal.
